evidence: The Composio page loads and explains managed OAuth apps, but its toolkit list is dynamic ("Loading toolkits..."). It does not name GitHub, a slug 'github', or a managed=true flag, so the claim cannot be verified from this page.

The page says you can register an OAuth app "under your personal account or under any organization you have administrative access to" and has a note that "A user or organization can own up to 100 OAuth apps."

The numbered steps are: open Settings, click Developer settings, click OAuth apps, click "New OAuth App". The form fields are "Application name", "Homepage URL", an optional "Application description", and "Authorization callback URL".
Step 10 says "Expire user access tokens is enabled by default." It also advises unchecking the box if the app does not yet support short-lived tokens.

The page says "When you create a new organization, OAuth app access restrictions are enabled by default." It also says that when restrictions are on, members "cannot authorize OAuth app access to organization resources" and can only "request owner approval."
The warning says "When an organization has not set up OAuth app access restrictions, any OAuth app authorized by an organization member can also access the organization's private resources."
The page says "The access token expires after eight hours, and the refresh token expires after six months without use."

The cited page loaded, but the fetched text was truncated before the 'Redirect URLs' section where the callback-matching, wildcard, and default-callback rules would appear. I could not verify this claim from the content retrieved.
